title: Midnight runtime triage + tooling checklist
content:
Goal: late-night sweep to catch regressions after the 03/11 canary. Mostly personal checklist + quick hypotheses to validate tomorrow morning.

Observations from canary (03/11 22:00–23:30):
- Sporadic p99 token spikes on smaller sequences (seq_len <= 64) on a subset of nodes. Not correlated with high CPU or memory on the node graph.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~8% for model variant rq-1.2 during steady traffic. Metrics show extra cache misses coincident with model rollout step.
- Two gRPC streams returned transient FailedPrecondition for ~45s window (region-eu-west-2). Retries succeeded; no data loss signaled.

Immediate quick triage steps (ordered):
1) Reproduce locally with replay tool: replay/trace-2026-03-11-canary.json focusing on seq_lens 16/32/64 and run in slow-mode to capture kernel traces.
   - Command: ./tools/replay --trace trace-2026-03-11-canary.json --filter "seq_len<=64" --slow 1
2) Check kernel driver log/sched traces for stuck CUDA launches during spikes. Collect nvprof/nsys snapshots for affected timestamp ranges.
3) Validate KV cache policy for rq-1.2: did rollout change insert/eviction thresholds? Inspect rollout config in PR 2145 and compare to prod-config.
4) Run a focused KV cache microbench against the new config: ./bench/kvbench --model rq-1.2 --ops mix --duration 120 --metrics p99,hit_rate
5) For the gRPC FailedPrecondition window, grep sidecar logs for network flaps and channel close reasons. Check LB logs and control-plane heartbeats.

Hypotheses (short notes):
- Hypothesis A: New kernel scheduling heuristic (PR 2145) defers small batch launches causing jitter on small sequences. Looks plausible because high-latency tails align with 'small batch' queueing periods.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache version mismatch during canary leads to conservative invalidation, lowering hit-rate. "Cold-writes" pattern observed in trace.
- Hypothesis C: Transient worker GC or resource reclamation (OOM kill/restart) on a subset of nodes triggered gRPC channel errors. Need to correlate with node restart events.

Data to collect (tomorrow morning):
- Timeline with token-level latency + kernel queue depth overlay (from 21:50–23:40)
- KV cache metrics (hit/miss, evictions) per-instance and per-model for rq-1.2
- Node-level events (restarts, docker restarts, host-level OOM killer) for region-eu-west-2
- Sidecar and LB logs for the 45s window

Short-term mitigations to consider if issue repeats in prod:
- Autoscaling: temporarily raise min-instances for variant rq-1.2 in EU to smooth variance.
- Rollback candidate: revert kernel scheduling changes behind an env flag. Canary rollback is faster than full revert.
- Increase KV cache expiry slightly to tolerate write storm during rollout (safe, but watch memory).

TODOs (assign to self unless flagged):
- [ ] Run replay and collect kernel flame for a 5–10 minute window (priority: high) — due 03/13 AM
- [ ] Validate rollout config differences and publish short note in #runtime-canary channel — due 03/13 AM
- [ ] Launch kvbench and collect hit/miss curves (priority: med) — due 03/13 noon
- [ ] Scan region-eu-west-2 node events and annotate suspicious hosts (priority: med) — due 03/13 noon
- [ ] Draft rollback playbook for kernel-sched toggle (include steps, impact, comms) — due 03/14

Small debugging snippets / commands to paste later:
- Replay (sh): ./tools/replay --trace /var/traces/trace-2026-03-11-canary.json --filter "seq_len<=64" --save-kernel kernel-clip.json
- KV bench (sh): ./bench/kvbench --model rq-1.2 --ops read:80,write:20 --concurrency 64 --duration 120 --out kv-2145.csv
- Fetch node events (k8s): kubectl get events -n inference --since=3h --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Node
- Tail sidecar logs (sh): sg tail sidecar region-eu-west-2 --since 1h | rg "FailedPrecondition|channel closed"

Notes to self / miscellaneous: 
- Remember to include per-token cost delta when proposing rollback (ops will ask).
- If we flip kernel-sched off, monitor small-sequence p95/p99 and also watch for batch throughput regressions.
- Quick runbook for oncall: if p99 > 1.2s for >5m, hit the rollback toggle, then escalate to platform-eng.

Unresolved questions:
- Why are only small seqs affected? Is it batching policy, or kernel pathing?
- Did the rollout enable a new quantization kernel on specific GPU types that misbehave at small seqs?
- Are the gRPC errors correlated with a specific LB back-end (ip/host)?

End-of-sesh quick summary (to paste in triage thread):
- Canary saw intermittent p99 spikes for short sequences and a small drop in KV hit-rate for rq-1.2. Investigating kernel-scheduling changes and KV rollout interactions. Reps: Jordan (me) + Mina to run experiments; will post updates 03/13 AM.
